# ContainerOptions

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Options for [`Container`](container.md). Intersects [`BorderedElementOptions`](bordered-element-options.md), so the `{ width, color }` border form works here (applied via `applyBorderedElementOptions`).

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

```typescript
type ContainerOptions = BorderedElementOptions & Partial<Omit<Pick<Container, ContainerOwnKey>, 'padding' | 'horizontalAlignment' | 'verticalAlignment' | 'width' | 'height'>> & {
    /** Fixed width. Accepts a length: `240`, `'8cm'`, or `{ value, unit }`. */
    width?: LengthInput;
    /** Fixed height. Accepts a length: `120`, `'1in'`, or `{ value, unit }`. */
    height?: LengthInput;
    /** Padding inside the border. Accepts `12`, `[h, v]`, `[l, t, r, b]` or `{ bottom: 12 }`. */
    padding?: ThicknessInput;
    /** Child placement. Accepts `'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch'`. */
    horizontalAlignment?: HorizontalAlignmentInput;
    /** Child placement. Accepts `'top' | 'middle' | 'bottom' | 'stretch'`. */
    verticalAlignment?: VerticalAlignmentInput;
}
```

### `backgroundColor`

```typescript
backgroundColor?: ColorInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Background fill. Accepts a palette token (`'slate-100'`) or hex.

### `border`

```typescript
border?: BorderInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Border widths, and optionally their colour.

Accepts a uniform width, a per-side object, or `{ width, color }`. Omitted sides are zero.

BonniePDF models widths and colours as separate properties (`border` + `borderColors`), so the colour-carrying form resolves to both. The `border` **property setter** deliberately never writes `borderColors` - a setter must not mutate a sibling - which is why this sugar lives here, in the options layer, and is applied by `applyBorderedElementOptions`.

### `borderColors`

```typescript
borderColors?: BorderColors | undefined
```

*optional*

Border colors for each side of the element

### `breakAllowed`

```typescript
breakAllowed?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Whether this element can be split across page boundaries. When false, the element is treated as atomic and will be moved to a new page rather than split. If it doesn't fit on a fresh page either, it renders anyway. Default is true.

### `captureName`

```typescript
captureName?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

Optional author-supplied name/key surfaced in the layout snapshot. Unset by default; a future capture API can populate it.

### `child`

```typescript
child?: IElement | undefined
```

*optional*

The element placed inside the container.

### `clipContent`

```typescript
clipContent?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

When `true` and [`BorderedElementBase.cornerRadius`](bordered-element-base.md#cornerradius) is positive, the container's content (background, border, and child) is clipped to the rounded-rectangle outline. This is what turns a rounded background into a true rounded-corner card: a full-bleed image or any overflowing child is masked to the rounded box rather than spilling past the corners. Defaults to `false`, so setting `cornerRadius` alone keeps the historical behaviour of a rounded fill/stroke with un-clipped content.

### `contentDirection`

```typescript
contentDirection?: ContentDirectionInput | undefined
```

Inline progression and paragraph base direction; omitted inherits.

### `cornerRadius`

```typescript
cornerRadius?: LengthInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Corner radius. Accepts a length: `6`, `'2mm'`, or `{ value, unit }`.

### `crispEdges`

```typescript
crispEdges?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

When `true`, the container's subtree renders inside a crisp-edge region: on SVG page export it emits `<g shape-rendering="crispEdges">`, so thin axis-aligned strokes and rectangles (grid/table lines, dividers) snap to the device pixel grid instead of being antialiased into a soft blur. It is a no-op on PDF output (the bytes are unchanged; crispness there is the viewer's job). Only wrap axis-aligned content — rounded rects, circles, diagonals, and text want antialiasing and will look jagged inside a crisp-edge region.

### `fillHeight`

```typescript
fillHeight?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

When `true`, the container takes the body content height left on the current page instead of sizing to its content. This is the primitive behind the header / body / footer page shape: the middle band is whatever the page chrome leaves over, a figure an author cannot compute up front because both templates are functions of the page number.

`height` wins outright — fill is only consulted when no height is pinned — and fill never *shrinks* content: a container whose child is taller than the space left keeps the child's height and paginates normally. Measurement is unaffected (it reports the natural content height, because a pure measure has no cursor to measure from); only arrangement expands.

Combines with `verticalAlignment`: the slack fill creates is exactly the space it gained, so `'bottom'` anchors content to the foot of the band.
